subject: dsa
title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
summary: From each cell you may step to a 4-directional neighbour only if it holds a strictly larger value. Each cell caches its own best path length, so it is computed once; the answer is the longest of these cached lengths.
problem: Find the length of the longest strictly increasing path in the matrix [[9,9,4],[6,6,8],[2,1,1]], moving up, down, left, or right. The grid shows the actual matrix values; the longest path runs 1, 2, 6, 9.

steps.caption: Goal: the longest strictly increasing path moving 4-directionally. Each cell caches its best length, so it is computed only once.
Start at the smallest value, the 1 at the bottom middle. On its own it is a path of length 1.
Step left to the 2 since 1 < 2. The path is now 1, 2 with length 2.
Step up to the 6 since 2 < 6. The path is now 1, 2, 6 with length 3.
Step up to the 9 since 6 < 9. 9 is a local max with no larger neighbour, so the path 1, 2, 6, 9 stops here.
The longest increasing path is 1, 2, 6, 9, so the answer is length 4.
